method: This compares the pcap-validation-pass s2c PCAP opcode histogram against the 55-opcode inbound receiver mapping. The raw observed-minus-mapped set is preserved, then the receiver-discovery pass worklist is scoped to receiver-family opcodes 0x012e..0x01f5.

dispatcherEvidence.summary: No single static factory table is documented. Prior option-2 analysis identifies two central packet routers that bind known opcodes to receiver application: FUN_004DC690 for the central high/low opcode router and FUN_004D8860 for the event-family router.

symbols.name: Option2_central_packet_dispatcher_FUN_004dc690
symbols.role: central packet router; high-opcode branch and low 0x00cc..0x00e5 fallthrough via actor->vftable[9]

symbols.name: Option2_event_family_dispatcher_FUN_004d8860
symbols.role: event-family packet router with dedicated per-opcode handler functions

worklistScope: Receiver-family candidate opcodes in the observed-unmapped set with 0x012e <= opcode <= 0x01f5. Low control/channel opcodes are excluded from the receiver-discovery pass's receiver-class walk but kept under excludedObservedButUnmapped.

scope_rationale.summary: After the pcap_validation.json reassembler fix grew the observed s2c histogram from 100 to 116 opcodes and observedButUnmappedRawCount from 68 to 83 (16 added, 1 removed), the 39-entry worklist[] is held at its current scope. None of the 16 newly added raw observed-but-unmapped opcodes qualify for worklist expansion under the existing scoping rules.

alreadyMappedInMatrixNotInInboundReceive: 0x0193 (count=9, Pattern D covered_pipeline via BCS-Y-0584 + BCS-Y-0990..0998 sub-dispatcher FUN_00578C90; matrix-covered, not a Receiver class so absent from receiver_opcode_map_inbound.json)
0x00e1 (count=3, Pattern C covered_pattern via BCS-Y-0540 + BCS-Y-0631 case 0xE1)
0x00e2 (count=8, Pattern C covered_pattern via BCS-Y-0540 + BCS-Y-0632 case 0xE2)
0x01cf (count=2, matrix s2c covered_pattern) - also misclassified by histogram
0x01ce (count=1, matrix c2s row FriendlistRequest; histogram s2c-side hit is direction misclassification)
0x01d3 (count=1, matrix c2s row for the OP_RX_GM_TICKET_STATE emitter; histogram s2c-side hit is direction misclassification)
stayDeferredPerTierC7: 0x01df (count=1, PlayerSearchInfoResultPacket - no internal RTTI attribution beyond the search-subsystem pass's catalog)

scopeRules: Stay-narrow precedent: documented the deferral of 0x01cf/0x01df/0x01e0 explicitly, on the grounds that no internal RTTI attribution exists for those receiver families. The newly observed singletons in that range fall under the same rationale. The deferral rests on the RTTI-attribution test alone.
recorded the deferral of this re-scope decision while completing mechanical citation cleanup.

None of the 16 newly added raw entries are in-range (0x012e..0x01a7) with count >= 5 AND lack existing matrix attribution. The only in-range new-raw entry above count 5 is 0x0193 (count=9), which is already covered_pipeline in the matrix per an earlier hygiene pass. The remaining 4 in-range new-raw entries (0x0153=2, 0x0189=1, 0x018a=1, 0x01a3=2, 0x01a7=1) are all count <= 2 singletons, already in worklist (the latter four) or already attributed (0x0153).

Signal-to-noise rationale (per task framework edge case): observedButUnmappedRawCount grew 68 -> 83 (+22%) but the newly added opcodes are dominated by either (a) opcodes that were already mapped via Pattern C/D in the matrix but not via inbound Receiver classes, or (b) count=1 singletons in resync-noise territory. Signal-to-noise degraded; stay-narrow is reinforced.
scope_rationale.worklistUnchangedReason: The 39-entry worklist continues to scope the receiver-discovery pass's receiver-class walk against opcodes 0x012e..0x01f5 with substantive pcap counts that lack receiver attribution. Expanding to include either (a) matrix-covered Pattern C/D opcodes that are not Receiver classes, or (b) post-0x01A7 singletons (which already documented as deferred) would dilute the receiver-class walk's purpose.
